anchors: Not every ignored file is regenerable
decision: Before removing a worktree, list its ignored files and diff every one that is not build output against the main checkout's copy; merge the worktree-only lines into the main copy (after copying it aside), copy in a file the main checkout lacks, and compare a secret-bearing file with cmp -s only.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: Step 4 called every gitignored file regenerable, 0 hits for a decision-log exception. GREEN opus and haiku diffed the decision log, copied the handover out, and left .venv/target alone in the control.

reopen_if: landed.py starts comparing ignored non-build files itself, or worktree removal stops deleting ignored files.
why: landed.py exits 0 over ignored files, and a gitignored decision log in a worktree held 93 lines while the same-named main copy held a condensed 83; removal would have deleted every dropped line, including each Reopen-if clause.

anchors: counts commits against where the session started, not origin
decision: ExitWorktree remove's 'Discarded N commits' counts commits the session's starting commit lacks, not commits missing from origin; judge a removal by landed.py before it and by merge-base --is-ancestor on a recorded tip after it, never by the count.

evidence.text: Observed 2026-11-08 in a session; CLI 2.1.319 code read: the refusal says 'commits that this session's starting commit lacks' and the count is rev-list --count <start>..HEAD. GREEN opus and haiku answered 'no commits lost' after a fetch plus ancestry check.

why: ExitWorktree reported 'Discarded 31 commits' for a worktree whose release was already on origin with CI green, because the local master the session started from lagged origin.

anchors: so a session editing this worktree right now leaves no hit
A behind count or the last commit's date says nothing about uncommitted files
a cwd link always holds the resolved path
decision: Before removing a dirty worktree or calling one stale, back the /proc cwd check with the dirty files' mtimes and a search of the session transcripts for the worktree path; a behind count or last-commit date says nothing about uncommitted files. The cwd grep takes the resolved path, since a cwd link holds the resolved path.

evidence.text: Measured on this repo: the skill's /proc cwd check from the main checkout returned 0 hits for a worktree a live session was editing (its claude process cwd was the main checkout); a positive control with a process cwd in the worktree returned 1; the new mtime and transcript commands listed the dirty file and the live transcripts; a process whose cwd was entered through a symlink matched the grep only by its realpath (0 vs 1). RED opus and haiku answered NONE to both quote-back questions on the pre-edit text.

reopen_if: Claude Code sessions start setting their process cwd to the worktree they edit, or a tool (landed.py, wtclean.py) starts detecting live sessions itself.
why: An agent session edits by absolute path from its launch directory, so the cwd check finds no process for a session editing the worktree right now; a worktree far behind origin with an old last commit was read as abandoned while a live session had edited it the same morning.

anchors: Inspect a worktree you may remove from OUTSIDE it.
decision: Step 4 inspects a worktree that may be removed from outside it: git -C <worktree> and absolute paths, or a subshell cd, never a bare cd, and the ignored-files listing uses git -C.

evidence.text: Opus and haiku quote-back on the new Step 4 answered with git -C from the new paragraph; asked directly, both baselines also chose git -C, so the change mainly removes the text's own 'inside it' cue.

reopen_if: The harness stops persisting a cd across Bash calls.
why: In an agent harness a successful cd persists as the session cwd, so the later removal ran from inside the directory it deleted: Windows refuses it, elsewhere the session is left in a deleted directory and its next git call exits 128. The old text said to list ignored files 'inside it', which invited the cd.

anchors: never of the repository the task is about
decision: A subagent dispatched with isolation worktree gets a worktree of the dispatching session's repository; for work in another repository, omit isolation and brief the agent to create its own worktree there with absolute paths, or pass the worktree as the Agent cwd where offered.

evidence.text: Queued lesson observed 2026-11-16: wrong-repo isolation worktree plus a leftover locked worktree. The Agent tool in the build used for this edit has no cwd parameter, which the text's 'where the tool offers the parameter' already allows for. Text-only RED probe on the pre-edit text answered NONE for which repository isolation uses.

reopen_if: The Agent tool gains a way to choose the repository for isolation worktree, or isolation is shown to follow the agent's cwd rather than the session's repository.
why: Dispatching from one repository for work in a sibling gave the agent a worktree of the wrong repository, a brief that did not match its tree, and a harness-locked worktree left behind to remove by hand.
